note: One shared `shared.ts` deployed as TWO workflows — one per Notion data source — so this file mirrors both deployments instead of one. Each deployment publishes its own `workflow.<kind>.ts` as `workflow.ts` alongside `shared.ts` verbatim, following the `whatsapp-slack-bridge` pattern. Republish both together whenever `shared.ts` changes.

deployments.name: sow-send-for-signing

trigger.webhook_url_note: This is the URL the Notion SOWs `Send for signing` button must POST to. It is NOT returned at get-workflow's top level — it lives at `triggers[0].details.webhook_url`. The `trigger_url` above is Zapier-internal and requires a JWT; do not point Notion at it.

connection_notes.notion_wf: work.flowers workspace connection. Never the `Knoxx | Dennis #2` connection (02b95b31-c152-8800-9036-1107e08f70da), which cannot see work.flowers databases.
connection_notes.esign_unofficial: `eSignatures.com (Unofficial)` — App236843CLIAPI, a by-invite private app. Used because its create_contract is the only one that accepts a single `markdown` body plus the name of the placeholder to inject it into. The PUBLIC `EsignaturesioCLIAPI` app has no markdown field (only a placeholder map) and is used by `esignatures-status-to-notion` for its triggers instead. The connection is pinned to App236843CLIAPI@1.0.0 while the app's latest is @1.0.1; that only matters for trigger claims, and this app is used for actions only.

esignatures.template_note: Templates are bare shells: a title, one `{{contract-body}}` placeholder, and signature fields eSignatures manages itself. So `template_id` and `placeholder_field_name` are the only template-coupled values.
esignatures.template_fix: The classic 'Send Project Addendum for Signing' Zap used the SOW template (6eaa0583) for addenda — a bug, confirmed with Dennis on 2026-08-04 and fixed here to 443d6bed. Both shells use the same `contract-body` placeholder, so the switch needed only the one constant.
esignatures.action_note: `test` is REQUIRED on App236843CLIAPI create_contract and its own default is "true" — it is set to false explicitly, or every run would produce a throwaway test contract. `save_as_draft: true` means nothing reaches a signer until a human sends the draft.
esignatures.result_shape: create_contract returns `{ data: [ { status: "queued", data: { contract: { id } } } ] }` — runAction supplies the outer `data` array and the app's envelope adds a SECOND `data` inside each row. The classic Zap's `gives[...]["data"]["contract"]["id"]` was addressing that inner `data`. Getting this wrong throws rather than writing a wrong id.

sows.name_note: Named `SOWs`, not "Scope of Work Database" as the classic Zap's parammap labelled it.
properties_read: Signatory Name (rollup via Counterparty signatory -> title)
Signatory Primary Email (rollup via Counterparty signatory -> email)
Override Email (Optional) (email) — wins over the rollup when set
SOW Name (rollup via Client SOW -> title)

properties_written: Status (status) = "In signing" — SOW flow only, skipped when the SOW has no Deal relation

notion.status_note: All three `Status` properties are type `status`, and `update_database_item` writes them fine — verified via `list-action-input-fields NotionCLIAPI write update_database_item --inputs '{"datasource":"..."}'`, which exposes `properties|||Status|||status`. An earlier note in spot-project-request-to-notion/README.md records status as unproven in this repo; that was an absence of local precedent, not a capability limit. No raw PATCH is needed for property writes here.
notion.rollup_note: `Signatory Name`, `Signatory Primary Email` and `SOW Name` are rollups, listed in the data source's `notAvailableInQuerySql`. They cannot be read via a SQL-mode query, so the page is fetched with `sdk.fetch` GET /v1/pages/{id} and the rollups read from `rollup.array[0]`.
notion.template_mode_note: Repo rule 5 does not apply — these workflows only UPDATE existing pages and never create any, so no data source default template is involved.
notion.markdown_export: The page body becomes the contract body via Notion's native `GET /v1/pages/{id}/markdown`. This replaces the classic Zap's `ae:577300` step — a hidden Zapier action extension that `runAction` cannot invoke at all (`ZAPIER_RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND_ERROR`). The native export is also more faithful than the Zapier block_children converter it used.

esignatures_mapping.name: eSignatures Mapping
esignatures_mapping.role: Written here (find-or-create on Page ID, then the Contract ID once the draft exists). Read by `esignatures-status-to-notion`, which only has a contract id to work from.

fields.Page ID: f1, string — the Notion SOW / Project Addendum page id
fields.Contract ID: f2, string — the eSignatures contract id
fields.Agreement Type: f3, labeled_string — "SOW" or "Project Addendum", written as { value, label }

esignatures_mapping.access_note: Read and written with `keyMode: "names"` via sdk.listTableRecords / createTableRecords / updateTableRecords, so the f-numbers never appear in code. Table calls consume no Zapier tasks.

live_runs.note: Verified 2026-08-04 with `run-durable` against purpose-made scratch records (since every real mapped record is a live client agreement). Scratch pages and their mapping rows were deleted afterwards; the three eSignatures drafts they produced are listed in the README for manual deletion.
